record.context_brief: Classical selection principles: equivalence and implication
record.original_question: For sets of reals, are the selection principles U_fin(Γ, Ω) and S_fin(Γ, Ω) equivalent, where Γ is the family of open γ-covers and Ω is the family of open ω-covers? If they are not equivalent, does the Hurewicz-type property U_fin(Γ, Γ) nevertheless imply S_fin(Γ, Ω)?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 ([24, Problems 1 and 2]). (1) Is Ufin(Γ, Ω) equivalent to Sfin(Γ, Ω)? (2) And if not, does Ufin(Γ, Γ) imply Sfin(Γ, Ω)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a set of real numbers (more generally, a topological space). For a family U of subsets of X, say that:
• U is an ω-cover of X if X is not a member of U and every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U;
• U is a γ-cover of X if U is infinite and every point of X belongs to all but finitely many members of U.

Let Γ denote the family of all open γ-covers of X and let Ω denote the family of all open ω-covers of X.

For collections A and B of covers of X, define the following selection principles:
• S_fin(A, B): for every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ℕ) with U_n ∈ A, there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the union ⋃_n F_n belongs to B.
• U_fin(A, B): for every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ℕ) with U_n ∈ A and such that no U_n contains a finite subcover of X, there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the family { ⋃ F_n : n ∈ ℕ } belongs to B.

Answer the following two questions:
(1) For every set of reals X, is the selection principle U_fin(Γ, Ω) equivalent to S_fin(Γ, Ω)?
(2) If they are not equivalent in general, does U_fin(Γ, Γ) imply S_fin(Γ, Ω) for every set of reals X?
artifact.status_search_result: The questions are among the long-standing problems concerning reversibility of arrows in the Scheepers diagram for selection principles, originally posed in the foundational work on combinatorics of open covers. Recent surveys and papers on the Scheepers diagram indicate that several arrows in the diagram remain not known to be reversible (with consistent non-reversibility for many), and no web-accessible source confirms a definitive resolution of these two specific questions. Hence the status is best described as unknown / likely still open.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles and proofs from the Book
status_evidence.snippet: Whether certain arrows of the [Scheepers] diagram are reversible remains unknown; all other arrows are at least consistently not reversible.
status_evidence.claim: Several reversibility questions in the Scheepers diagram (including those relating U_fin and S_fin variants) are still recorded as open or only consistently resolved.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems (Tsaban)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems in selection principles, including problems originally raised by Just, Miller, Scheepers, and Szeptycki.
status_evidence.claim: The questions about equivalence of U_fin(Γ,Ω) with S_fin(Γ,Ω) and whether U_fin(Γ,Γ) implies S_fin(Γ,Ω) appear among the milestone open problems.
